journey.description: The name of the app-map journey whose steps reach the risky code.

path.description: Exactly as in the endpoint list, such as /payments.

body.description: The JSON request body as a template with placeholders.

correlateBy.description: The request body field whose value identifies the request; a field of a nested object as a.b, such as address.street.

responseField.description: Only when the effect row holds an ID the app makes itself: the field of the app's JSON answer that carries it, such as id. Empty when the effect holds the correlateBy value.

table.description: Where processing one request leaves exactly one row, in the database of the service that does the work.

column.description: The column of that table holding the correlateBy value, or the responseField value when there is one.

reset.description: TRUNCATE, DELETE and UPDATE statements that put every database the journey writes to back to its starting state.

rules.description: What the data must keep once every request has been processed, each as SQL that returns the rows breaking it.

id.description: A kebab-case name, such as stock-never-negative.

why.description: First: what must hold, and which part of the journey keeps it.

sql.description: Then one SELECT that returns the rows breaking it, and none in a correct run; only tables of one database.

why.description: How this traffic reaches the risky code, in one or two sentences.
